when: an administrator approves it
then: the account is active and the person can sign in

given: a pending account and a person who is not an administrator
when: that person tries to approve it
then: it is refused and the account stays pending

when: its owner makes any request other than asking for their own status
then: it is refused
notes: Was 'sign-in is refused' before decision 24: the person can now sign in at Keycloak, and our API holds them.

when: an administrator deactivates it and gives a reason
then: the account is deactivated and its owner can no longer sign in

when: an administrator deactivates it without a reason
then: it is refused and the account stays active

when: that administrator tries to deactivate it
then: it is refused
notes: An administrator cannot deactivate themselves. The rule is not written in the ontology yet.

when: an administrator reinstates it
then: the account is active and its owner can sign in again

given: each role (administrator, auditor, project manager, engineer) and a person who is not a member of the project
when: each makes every command and read the role is not allowed
then: the server refuses every one
notes: This is the requirement's own measure: a refusal on every command and every read, for each role.

given: a screen that hides a button the role may not use
when: the request is sent directly to the server
then: the server still refuses it

when: its owner asks for their own status
then: it says the account is waiting for approval

given: a person the system does not know, signed in through the identity provider
when: they make their first request
then: a pending account exists for them

given: a person who already has an account
when: they make another request
then: no second account is created

given: an approved person with an identity provider account
when: they sign in through the identity provider
then: they can use the product

when: they sign out
then: the product no longer accepts their session and asks them to sign in again

when: they open their profile
then: it shows their name and account role

given: a request with no token, an expired token, or a token not issued by the identity provider
when: it is made to any protected route
then: it is refused
notes: Each of the three is its own case in the test.

when: they try to change an account's role through Playground
then: there is no way to do it

given: the identity provider account that the backend uses
when: its rights are listed
then: it cannot assign roles
notes: Needs checking against what Keycloak's admin roles allow.

given: an active account whose owner holds a valid token
when: an administrator deactivates it
then: the owner's next request is refused
notes: Needs our API to check the account on every request, and the person's Keycloak sessions to end.

when: its records are inspected
then: all of its data is still there

given: a deactivated person with an evaluation running
when: time passes
then: the evaluation reaches its end
